report.summary: Parsed bus.py chunk 1: module docstring, constants, hash/identity/secret scan functions. 7 public symbols enumerated, 20+ claims checked.
risks: _resolve_store | medium | Uses Path.cwd() for relative paths; if cwd changes, council writes could go to unexpected locations. | Verify that caller always passes absolute base_dir or that cwd is stable.
_ACTOR_RE | low | Pattern allows 'council.a.b.c:1' but ADR-010 mentions 'council.<vendor>.<model>'; vendor namespace may be violated if model contains dots. | Confirm ADR-010 specification.
MAX_CONTENT_CHARS | medium | Fail-closed ceiling at 200k chars; if a turn exceeds this, behavior (raise? truncate?) not defined in this chunk. | Check append_round for enforcement.
_scan_turn | medium | Function signature present but body truncated; secret floor scan logic incomplete in this chunk. | Review full implementation in later chunk.
todos: Verify that _scan_turn implements the docstring's claim about re-scanning receipts.
Check that _resolve_store is called with absolute paths in production to avoid cwd dependency.
Ensure that MAX_CONTENT_CHARS enforcement raises a clear error.
Confirm that _APPEND_CACHE is invalidated on file size/mtime change (not in this chunk).

claims.text: Every line carries the SHA of the line before it, so a flipped byte or a deleted INTERIOR line breaks the chain and verify_chain NAMES the offending 1-indexed line.
claims.why: verify_chain is not defined in this chunk; the hash chaining mechanism is partially present (_entry_sha) but the chain linking is not shown.

claims.text: TAIL truncation (any prefix of a valid chain is itself a valid chain) is caught only against the head/count ANCHOR persisted beside the transcript and re-checked on every verify.
claims.why: Anchor file mechanism (anchor_path) exists but verify_chain and anchor check are not in this chunk.

claims.text: This is dcouncil/1. It deliberately REIMPLEMENTS memstore.py's two-SHA discipline instead of importing it, and it must never write to the memory ledger.
claims.why: ENTRY_VERSION is 'dcouncil/1'; _resolve_store explicitly refuses paths under memory/; no import from memstore.

claims.text: Any store path under <repo>/memory/ is refused loudly by _resolve_store.
claims.why: _resolve_store raises ValueError if resolved path is under _FORBIDDEN_STORE_DIR.

claims.text: body_sha -- sha256 over json.dumps(canonical_body, sort_keys=True, separators=(",",":"), ensure_ascii=True) where canonical_body is the record MINUS the four position/identity fields ts, prev, entry_sha, id (and body_sha itself).
claims.why: _body_sha uses canonical_body_json which uses those exact separators and sort_keys; canonical_body excludes _NON_BODY_FIELDS (ts, prev, entry_sha, id, body_sha).

claims.text: entry_sha -- sha256(prev + "\0" + body_sha + "\0" + ts), the chain link. Genesis prev is None and folds in as "" (unambiguous: a real prev is always a 64-hex digest).
claims.why: _entry_sha computes sha256((prev or '') + '\0' + body_sha + '\0' + ts).

claims.text: a turn's id is entry_sha[:16], not body_sha[:16]
claims.why: id assignment logic not present in this chunk.

claims.text: there is NO dedupe. A council transcript is a log of EVENTS: two participants may legitimately emit byte-identical bodies, and deduping the second away would erase a voice from the record.
claims.why: No deduplication logic visible; claim about absence cannot be verified from code present.

claims.text: append_round takes a whole round's turns in ANY completion order, sorts them by the vendor-namespaced actor id, assigns seq at chain time, and stamps ONE chain timestamp for the round.
claims.why: append_round is not defined in this chunk.

claims.text: The same fixture responses delivered in reversed completion order therefore produce a byte-identical chain head
claims.why: Depends on append_round implementation not present.

claims.text: PATH channel: every evidence path, INDIVIDUALLY.
claims.why: _scan_paths iterates over paths and calls secret_floor_rule with each path individually.

claims.text: CONTENT channel: the turn content, every ref, and every metadata string, each scanned on its own -- never over the assembled turn.
claims.why: _scan_turn is truncated; the full list of scanned strings is not shown. _scan_texts iterates over a list of texts, but the caller's logic is incomplete.

claims.text: This runs on OUTBOUND turns and, critically, on INBOUND vendor responses BEFORE they are chained
claims.why: Call site of _scan_turn not present.

claims.text: A hit REFUSES the turn -- no redact-and-send, no redact-and-store. In its place a status='refused' receipt is chained naming ONLY the rule label
claims.why: Refusal logic not present in this chunk.

claims.text: The receipt is re-scanned before it is written; if the identity fields themselves carry the secret the receipt degrades to an anonymous one rather than smuggling the credential onto the very path meant to be safe.
claims.why: Re-scan logic not present.

claims.text: withheld (paths an egress lane declined to send) is scanned with the CONTENT channel only, never the path channel.
claims.why: Scanning logic for withheld not present; _scan_turn incomplete.

claims.text: EVERY REQUESTED PARTICIPANT PRODUCES EXACTLY ONE CHAINED TURN PER ROUND -- content, refused, unavailable with a machine reason, or budget_exhausted.
claims.why: Turn production logic not present.

claims.text: A two-vendor council must never render identically to a four-vendor one.
claims.why: No rendering or comparison logic present.

claims.text: A key outside this set is REFUSED loudly, never dropped: a silently dropped field lets two semantically distinct turns canonicalise to the same body and hands the caller a success id for a turn never recorded.
claims.why: Key validation logic not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Two participants citing 'the file' may have been shown different bytes; without this the transcript records a citation that cannot be reproduced.
claims.why: evidence_ref includes both path and sha256 of the exact bytes, enabling reproduction.

claims.text: council_id is filename-safe by validation, not by sanitising: a silently rewritten id would point two councils at one transcript.
claims.why: _check_council_id validates against _COUNCIL_ID_RE and raises ValueError; no sanitisation is performed.

claims.text: The head/count anchor beside the transcript. Separate file on purpose: the chain walk cannot detect tail truncation from a truncated file alone.
claims.why: anchor_path returns a separate .anchor.json file path.

claims.text: PATH channel, one path at a time -- so a hit is attributable to one path and a diff that ADDS .env cannot hide inside a blob.
claims.why: _scan_paths iterates over each path individually and calls secret_floor_rule per path.

claims.text: CONTENT channel, one string at a time. path='' here is correct and is NOT the forbidden whole-prompt call: the path tier is run separately over every evidence path above, so it is never skipped.
claims.why: _scan_texts calls secret_floor_rule with path='' and text=t, and _scan_paths handles paths separately.

observations.what: Module docstring makes extensive claims about behavior not yet implemented in this chunk (append_round, verify_chain, refusal logic).
_scan_turn is incomplete; its signature is present but body is truncated at end of chunk.
Public symbols canonical_body, canonical_body_json are exposed; _body_sha and _entry_sha are private. Module docstring mentions verify_chain but it is not defined.
_FORBIDDEN_STORE_DIR is set to ROOT / 'memory' but the module docstring says 'any store path under <repo>/memory/' is refused; _resolve_store uses resolved path comparison, which is robust.
The constant _ACTOR_RE is defined but not used in this chunk; actor_id constructs the string without regex validation.
